literal.prompt: После какого из этих царей на московский престол взошёл его сын Алексей?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The retained Presidential Library collection states that Mikhail Fedorovich’s son Alexei Mikhailovich and grandson Fyodor successively occupied the Moscow throne (L326). It calls them tsars; the target therefore asks a distinct father-to-son succession fact. The four options are consistently declined ruler names; Mikhail is the only supported father of the Alexei described.

literalGroups.literal: В XVII веке московский престол последовательно занимали Михаил Фёдорович, его сын Алексей Михайлович и внук Михаила Фёдор Алексеевич. Поэтому правильный ответ — Михаил Романов.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The retained collection lists the sequence as Mikhail Fedorovich’s son Alexei Mikhailovich and grandson Fyodor Alexeevich (L326). This grounds both the father-to-son succession and the subsequent grandson, without using the 1613 election or end of Smuta as the tested MAIN.

literalGroups.literal: После свержения Лжедмитрия I боярство выдвинуло Василия Шуйского на престол; в 1610 году его свергли.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The retained official library account says that after False Dmitry I was deposed, the boyars put Vasily Shuisky on the throne, and that Shuisky was deposed in 1610 (L53-L56).

literalGroups.literal: В июне 1605 года Лжедмитрия I признали царём в Москве; позднее его свергли и убили.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The retained official library account says False Dmitry I entered Moscow in June 1605, was recognized as tsar by the people and part of the nobility, and was later deposed and killed (L53).

The retained Romanov collection identifies Mikhail Fedorovich as tsar and gives his life dates as 1596–1645 (L346). This remains a concrete extra fact about the correct option beyond the revised prompt and key.

literalGroups.literal: Борис Годунов стал первым русским царём, получившим престол по избранию, а не по наследству.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The retained official library article says Boris Godunov became the first tsar to receive the throne by election rather than inheritance (L51), a specific and useful fact about this distractor.

absoluteDifficulty.ground: This is an identifiable dynastic succession fact rather than a date or role from Mikhail’s 1613 election. A player familiar with Russian history may know that Alexei followed his father Mikhail; a player outside the topic has no patronymic clue in the prompt and cannot solve it from broad adult knowledge alone. The distractors are earlier Russian rulers/claimants from the same broad period, not absurd options.
